headline: Gilding edges Manby 5-4 and cites a packed calendar
standfirst: Andrew Gilding won his first Grand Slam match in a ninth-leg decider and spoke about age, fatigue and finances.
body: Andrew Gilding secured his first win of the Grand Slam of Darts, beating fellow Englishman Charlie Manby 5-4 in a ninth-leg decider that ended Manby's hopes of qualification.

Neither player was at his best. Gilding called it "a big struggle" and said his experience told in the final leg. He expects Manby, who is the younger man, to handle such moments better as he gets more stage time, according to Dartsnews.

The 55-year-old, who won the UK Open in March, said he usually plays better in the first half of the year. His 2026 included a first Players Championship title and another final, but results have been less consistent since. He suggested age and a tough calendar may be factors, mentioning a sore back that he said is not a serious injury.

Gilding said the schedule leaves him little choice. He plays nearly every Players Championship event and many European Tour dates, and explained that he is not in a position to pick and choose where he plays. Fatigue builds as the year goes on, he said, before the break after Christmas lets him recover.
The financial pressure was part of the picture: the headline quote from Dartsnews has him saying he never saved that much.
The result keeps Gilding's own campaign alive in Wolverhampton.
